mcqs.q: Amelogenesis is the process of enamel formation carried out by:
mcqs.explain: Amelogenesis is the formation of enamel by ameloblasts, beginning shortly after dentinogenesis at the advanced bell stage.

mcqs.q: Amelogenesis begins:
opts: Shortly AFTER dentinogenesis (the first dentin layer forms first)
mcqs.explain: Enamel matrix formation begins against the newly formed dentin — amelogenesis follows dentinogenesis at the advanced bell stage.

mcqs.q: The two main stages of amelogenesis are:
mcqs.explain: Amelogenesis involves enamel matrix deposition and then mineralization/maturation of the matrix.

mcqs.q: The five functional stages of the ameloblast life cycle are:
mcqs.explain: The IEE cells pass through presecretory, secretory, transitional, maturation and protective stages.

mcqs.q: During the MORPHOGENETIC phase:
opts: The shape of the crown is determined
mcqs.explain: In the morphogenetic phase the crown shape is determined; the IEE induces the dental papilla to form odontoblasts.

mcqs.q: In the DIFFERENTIATION phase, ameloblasts:
opts: Elongate, shift their nuclei proximally and can no longer divide
mcqs.explain: As IEE cells differentiate into ameloblasts they elongate, nuclei shift proximally, organelles move distally, and the cells can no longer divide.

mcqs.q: The very FIRST layer of enamel formed by ameloblasts is:
mcqs.explain: The initial layer of enamel formed against the dentin contains no enamel rods (rodless); rods appear once Tomes' processes develop.

mcqs.q: Tomes' process is:
opts: A conical process at the distal ameloblast end that forms the enamel rods
mcqs.explain: Tomes' process is a conical process at the distal end of the ameloblast; it interdigitates with the enamel ('picket fence') and forms rods and inter-rod enamel.

mcqs.q: When Tomes' processes are lost at the end of the secretory stage, the last enamel formed is:
mcqs.explain: As Tomes' processes are lost, the last formed layers of enamel are rodless/prismless (like the first layer).

mcqs.q: Each enamel rod is formed by the contribution of:
mcqs.explain: Each rod is formed by four ameloblasts: the head by one ameloblast and the tail by three.

mcqs.q: In the TRANSITIONAL stage, what happens to the ameloblast population?
opts: About 50% die by apoptosis (programmed cell death)
mcqs.explain: In the transitional stage the ameloblasts shorten, organelles are reduced, and ~50% of the population is lost by apoptosis.

mcqs.q: During MATURATION, there is:
opts: A massive influx of calcium/phosphate and loss of amelogenin and water
mcqs.explain: Maturation features a massive influx of calcium and phosphate with selective loss of enamel proteins (mainly amelogenin) and water.

mcqs.q: Ruffled-ended ameloblasts:
opts: Spend ~80% of the time in this form and add inorganic material to the enamel
mcqs.explain: Ruffled-ended ameloblasts (cell ~80% of its time) incorporate inorganic material; smooth-ended ameloblasts (~20%) remove protein fragments and water.

mcqs.q: Smooth-ended ameloblasts function to:
opts: Remove protein fragments and water from the enamel matrix
mcqs.explain: Smooth-ended ameloblasts (~20% of the time) mediate the exit of protein fragments and water from the enamel matrix.

mcqs.q: In the PROTECTIVE stage, the ameloblasts and remaining enamel-organ layers form the:
mcqs.explain: In the protective stage, ameloblasts become short cuboidal cells that, with the other layers, form the reduced enamel epithelium covering the enamel until eruption.

mcqs.q: Amelogenesis imperfecta is:
opts: A genetic group of conditions affecting enamel structure/appearance
mcqs.explain: Amelogenesis imperfecta is a group of genomic conditions affecting enamel structure/clinical appearance, causing discoloration and (in severe cases) hypomineralized enamel.

mcqs.q: The basement membrane between the IEE and odontoblasts:
opts: Disintegrates after dentinogenesis and before amelogenesis
mcqs.explain: The delicate basement membrane between the IEE and odontoblasts disintegrates after dentinogenesis and before amelogenesis begins.

mcqs.q: The 'picket-fence' appearance during enamel formation is due to:
opts: Tomes' processes interdigitating with the forming enamel
mcqs.explain: Tomes' processes interdigitate with the surface of the forming enamel, giving a characteristic picket-fence appearance.

mcqs.q: Mineralization of enamel proceeds:
opts: Progressively as more matrix is deposited, from cusp toward cervical areas
Backwards from surface to dentin only
mcqs.explain: Initial enamel is formed and calcified as further increments are added; matrix deposition and mineralization proceed across the sides and cervical areas of the crown.

mcqs.q: Ameloblasts lose their ability to divide:
mcqs.explain: Once the IEE cells differentiate into ameloblasts (differentiation phase), they can no longer divide.

saqs.q: Define amelogenesis and its two stages.
saqs.a: Enamel formation by ameloblasts (after dentinogenesis at the advanced bell stage). Two stages: enamel matrix secretion and mineralization/maturation.

saqs.q: List the five stages of the ameloblast life cycle.
What is Tomes' process and its function?
saqs.a: A conical process at the distal end of the secretory ameloblast that interdigitates with the enamel ('picket fence'); it forms the rods and inter-rod enamel. Its loss leaves rodless enamel.

saqs.q: How many ameloblasts form one enamel rod?
saqs.a: Four ameloblasts — the head by 1 and the tail by 3.

saqs.q: Describe the maturation stage of amelogenesis.
saqs.a: Massive calcium/phosphate influx with loss of amelogenin and water; ameloblasts modulate between ruffled-ended (80%, add mineral) and smooth-ended (20%, remove protein/water).

saqs.q: What happens in the transitional and protective stages?
saqs.a: Transitional: organelles reduced, ~50% of ameloblasts die by apoptosis. Protective: cells become short cuboidal and form the reduced enamel epithelium until eruption.
A group of genetic (genomic) conditions affecting enamel structure and appearance, causing discoloration and, in severe cases, hypomineralized enamel.
